subject: science
intro: The rate of a reaction is how fast it happens. Reactions occur when particles collide with enough energy. Anything that makes collisions happen more often or with more energy speeds up the reaction. Raising the temperature makes particles move faster, so they collide more often and harder, speeding up the reaction. Increasing the concentration (more particles in the same space) makes collisions more frequent, also speeding it up. Increasing surface area of a solid exposes more particles to collide. So temperature, concentration, and surface area all affect reaction rate.

items.prompt: Why does raising the temperature speed up a reaction?

steps: Reactions happen when particles collide with enough energy.
Higher temperature makes particles move faster, so they collide more often and with more energy.
More frequent, more energetic collisions speed up the reaction.
solution.answer: Higher temperature makes particles move faster, so they collide more often and harder, speeding up the reaction.

items.prompt: How does increasing the concentration of reactants affect the reaction rate?

steps: Concentration is how many particles are packed in a space.
More particles in the same space collide more often.
More frequent collisions speed up the reaction, so higher concentration increases the rate.
solution.answer: Higher concentration means more frequent collisions, which speeds up the reaction.

items.prompt: A solid reacts faster when it is ground into a powder than as a single lump. Explain why.

steps: A reaction happens where particles can collide, at the solid's surface.
Grinding the solid into powder greatly increases its surface area.
More surface area exposes more particles to collide, so the reaction goes faster.
solution.answer: Grinding increases the surface area, exposing more particles to collide, so the reaction is faster.

items.prompt: What is the rate of a reaction?

steps: The rate of a reaction is how fast the reaction happens.

items.prompt: Two identical reactions are run, one in a fridge and one in a warm room. Which goes faster and why?

steps: Temperature affects how fast particles move and collide.
The warm-room reaction has faster-moving particles that collide more often and harder.
So the warm-room reaction goes faster than the cold fridge one.
solution.answer: The warm-room reaction goes faster, because warmer particles collide more often and with more energy.

items.prompt: Explain, using collisions, why both higher temperature and higher concentration speed up a reaction.

steps: Reactions need particles to collide with enough energy.
Higher temperature makes particles collide more often and with more energy; higher concentration makes them collide more often.
Both increase the number (and energy) of effective collisions, so both speed up the reaction.
solution.answer: Both increase effective collisions: temperature adds frequency and energy, concentration adds frequency, so both speed the reaction.
